21: make run        # docker compose up -d
22: make stop       # docker compose down

25: make acp        # docker compose up -d opencode-acp

30: make generic    # docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker
31: ```

36:

38: # Start all servers
39: docker compose up -d

43: 
44: # Check

46: ```

52: ```

57: ISSUE_URL=https://github.com/tbrandenburg/pyrag/issues/30 \
58:   GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) \
59:   docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue
60: ```
61: 
62: ### Generic worker (one-shot, clone + exec)
63: 
64: ```bash
65: # Mount a local script and execute it in the cloned repo:
66: docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
67:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/tbrandenburg/pyrag.git \
68:   -e ISSUE=42 \
69:   -v ./workflows/issue-resolution/.opencode:/opencode-config:ro \
70:   -v ./my-script.sh:/script.sh:ro \

76:   -e ISSUE=42 \

# opencode-container

Docker images for running [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) in various serving modes — HTTP server, web UI, ACP protocol bridge, and ephemeral issue-processing workers.

## Quickstart

```bash
# 1. Build all images
make build

# 2. Start the headless HTTP server
make serve

# 3. Verify it's running
curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
```

**Prerequisites**: [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) (with Compose v2), [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (for runner containers).

## Containers

| Container | Mode | Port | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `opencode-serve` | `serve` | 4096 | Headless HTTP server with web UI + REST API + OpenAPI doc |
| `opencode-web` | `web` | 4098 | Same as serve with auto-instantiated project instance |
| `opencode-acp` | `acp` | 4097 | ACP (Agent Client Protocol) JSON-RPC server over stdio, bridged to TCP via socat |
| `opencode-issue-processor` | `run` | — | Batch: iterate all open issues from configured repos, piped into `opencode run` |
| `opencode-plan-issue` | `run` | — | One-shot: clone a repo, analyze an issue, post implementation plan as comment |
| `opencode-generic-worker` | `run` | — | Clone a repo, bootstrap opencode config, execute a mounted script or inline command |

## Architecture

### Why this design?

OpenCode supports three runtime modes — `serve` (HTTP API), `web` (HTTP + instant project), and `acp` (JSON-RPC stdio) — plus a `run` mode for one-off agent invocations. Each mode has different network and lifecycle needs:

- **`serve` / `web`** are long-running HTTP servers. They bind to a port, persist data in Docker volumes, and expose health-check and API endpoints.
- **`acp`** communicates over stdio using JSON-RPC 2.0. To make it accessible over the network inside Docker, `socat` bridges the stdio protocol to a TCP socket. This allows external ACP clients to connect without modifying the opencode process.
- **`run` containers** (`issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker`) are ephemeral. They clone a git repo, perform a task via `opencode run`, and exit. They use Docker's `profiles: [manual]` so they are never started by `docker compose up` — only via explicit `docker compose run --rm`.

### Which container do I pick?

| You want to... | Use this container |
|---|---|
| Run a headless OpenCode server with a web UI | `opencode-serve` |
| Run OpenCode web with an auto-created project | `opencode-web` |
| Connect an ACP client (e.g., Cline, continue.dev) | `opencode-acp` |
| Process all open issues from one or more repos | `opencode-issue-processor` |
| Analyze a single issue and post a plan | `opencode-plan-issue` |
| Run a custom script inside a cloned repo | `opencode-generic-worker` |

### Volume sharing strategy

All containers that persist configuration or data share two named volumes:

| Volume | Mount point | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `opencode-data` | `/root/.local/share/opencode` | Session data, project history |
| `opencode-config` | `/root/.config/opencode` | Global opencode config, agent definitions |

This means data and configuration persist across container restarts and can be shared between server and runner containers.

### `profiles: [manual]` pattern

Containers with `profiles: [manual]` are excluded from `docker compose up`. They must be launched explicitly with `docker compose run --rm`. This prevents long-running server mode from accidentally starting ephemeral batch containers.

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Affected containers | Required | Default | Security note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` | `opencode-serve`, `opencode-web` | no | `changeme` | Basic auth password for HTTP endpoints |
| `GH_TOKEN` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | yes (for GitHub operations) | — | Interpolated by calling shell via `$(gh auth token)` — never read into agent context |
| `ISSUE_URL` | `plan-issue` | yes | — | Full GitHub issue URL (e.g. `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/42`) |
| `REPO_URL` | `generic-worker` | yes | — | Git clone URL |
| `ISSUE` | `generic-worker` | no | empty | Issue number, passed as env to child command |
| `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` | `generic-worker` (script) | no | `/opencode-config` | Directory to copy config from when bootstrapping |
| `WORK_DIR` | `generic-worker` (script) | no | `/repo` | Clone destination directory |
| `OPENCODE_GLOBAL_DIR` | `generic-worker` (script) | no | `/root/.config/opencode` | Target directory for bootstrapped config |

## Network

| Container | Port | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| `opencode-serve` | 4096 | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
| `opencode-web` | 4098 | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
| `opencode-acp` | 4097 | None (stdio → TCP via socat) |

## Commands

```bash
make build      # docker compose build
make run        # docker compose up -d (all servers)
make stop       # docker compose down
make serve      # docker compose up -d opencode-serve
make web        # docker compose up -d opencode-web
make acp        # docker compose up -d opencode-acp
make logs       # docker compose logs -f
make clean      # docker compose down --remove-orphans -v
make process    # docker compose run --rm opencode-issue-processor
make plan       # docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue
make generic    # docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker
make lint       # shellcheck on all .sh files
make test       # Run integration tests for all containers
```

## Usage

### Server containers (long-running)

```bash
# Start all servers
make run

# Start individual server
docker compose up -d opencode-serve

# Health check
curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health

# View logs
make logs

# Stop everything
make stop
```

### Issue processor (batch, then exit)

```bash
GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) make process
```

The processor iterates all open issues from configured repos (see `process-issues.sh`), running `opencode run` on each.

### Issue planner (one-shot, then exit)

```bash
ISSUE_URL=https://github.com/tbrandenburg/pyrag/issues/30 \
  GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) \
  make plan
```

Clones the repo, analyzes the issue, and posts an implementation plan as a GitHub comment.

### Generic worker (one-shot, clone + exec)

```bash
# Mount a local script and execute it in the cloned repo:
docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
  -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/tbrandenburg/pyrag.git \
  -e ISSUE=42 \
  -v ./workflows/issue-resolution/.opencode:/opencode-config:ro \
  -v ./my-script.sh:/script.sh:ro \
  /script.sh

  -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/tbrandenburg/pyrag.git \
  -e ISSUE=42 \
  sh -c 'echo "Issue: $ISSUE" && cat README.md'

### `--help` passthrough

```bash
docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help
docker compose run --rm opencode-web --help
```

## Rules & Security

- Only `opencode serve` and `opencode web` support `--port`, `--hostname`, `--cors`, `--mdns`
- `opencode acp` communicates over stdio using JSON-RPC 2.0 — socat bridges it to TCP for container access
- `opencode run` is used for ephemeral batch/plan containers — needs a git repo and provider credentials
- **Never hardcode `GH_TOKEN`** in Dockerfiles or scripts. Use `$(gh auth token)` from the calling shell.
- All containers use `node:22-slim` base image with `opencode-ai` npm package and `gh` CLI installed via tarball from `cli/cli` releases
- `profiles: [manual]` services must be run with `docker compose run --rm` — not started by `docker compose up`
- Container `CMD` / `ENTRYPOINT` scripts use `set -euo pipefail` and validate required environment variables with meaningful error messages before proceeding

## Testing

```bash
make build    # Build all images first
make test     # Run integration tests
```

- `--help` passthrough for `opencode-serve` and `opencode-web`
- Required env-var validation for `generic-worker`
